newsitem.title: BOSNIA: EU deal signed to restore Bosnia's telephones.
newsitem.headline: EU deal signed to restore Bosnia's telephones.

text.p: The Bosnian Moslem-Croat federation signed an agreement on Monday with the European Union for the reconstruction and reintegration of the country's divided telephone network, EU officials said.
The EU project will link telephone systems between Serb and Moslem-Croat territories which have been divided since war erupted in Bosnia in 1992.
Moslem-Croat federation leaders earlier refused to sign the agreement because they said the project could undermine Bosnia's sovereignty by creating two largely separate telephone systems.
Bosnian Serb representatives had already signed the memorandum of understanding and the federation agreed to the deal on Monday after coming under heavy international pressure.
The United States and European powers had set a July 15 deadline for the two entities to agree to the EU project or face unspecified penalties.

The EU has selected Alcatel and the French military to help manage the project and provide technical equipment, including a microwave radio relay network, a basic radio relay network for Serb territory, cables, switches and access networks.
Construction work was due to begin immediately and some equipment had already been delivered, EU officials said.
Currently, Bosnia's Serb entity is part of neighbouring Yugoslavia's telephone network and calls between Serb territory and the Moslem-Croat federation are impossible.
A utility company in neighbouring Croatia controls the telephone network in Croat areas in the federation.

EU ambassador Donato Chiarini said the project was of "crucial importance" to rebuilding the country's economy and restoring links between the Serb and Moslem-Croat entities that comprise post-war Bosnia.
The memorandum should provide a framework for an agreement between the two entities, Chiarini told reporters.
Federation representatives in Sarajevo have to use satellite phones to speak to their Serb counterparts in Pale, 16 km (10 miles) away.
The first disbursement under the agreement will supply equipment worth 16 million German marks ($9 million), the EU said in a statement.
Edhem Bicakcic, federation prime minister, said he was optimistic the project could be finished by the autumn.
"I think all neccessary work can be completed by the end of September, and then we shall have one united telecommunication system in Bosnia," Bicakcic said.

EU officials were more cautious, saying links between Sarajevo and the Pale region to the east should be restored before October. The whole telephone project should be finished by the end of the year.
Western diplomats said the telecommunications project was vital for attracting foreign investment and promoting trade between the two entities.
